newsitem.title: UK: Nomura launches new English football share index.
newsitem.headline: Nomura launches new English football share index.

text.p: Japanese bank Nomura International on Thursday unveiled a share index of leading English football clubs and, at the same time, launched financial derivatives on that index.

The index will expand to cover other premier league clubs whose shares become publicly available -- Sunderland FC is soon to be floated. Teams will be struck off if they are relegated from the English Football Association's premier league.
The warrants launched in conjunction with the index allow investors to take a highly-leveraged position on those clubs' overall off-field performance.

Warrant holders can buy the index at a future date at a price which has been set. Any gains in the underlying clubs's share price from today will accrue to the warrant holders at a faster rate than could be achieved by buying the actual shares.
The group of nine listed clubs in the new index include Manchester United, the largest club in Britain with a market capitalisation of 362 million stg.
Nomura has an outstanding index, launched in August, which tracks the prices of all quoted British football stocks, not just English premier league teams.
That index is up by 22 percent since its launch. From the start of the year the increase is 160 percent, Nomura's chief equity strategist Nick Knight told Reuters.
Knight said the gains were due to factors including better attendances and a new television contract, which showed football was an "emerging sub-sector of the leisure industry".
